target_claim: Let G be a finite non-abelian group, let Z(G) denote its center, and let Γ(G) be the graph whose vertex set is G \ Z(G), with two vertices x and y adjacent exactly when xy ≠ yx. A subset of the vertices is independent when its elements are pairwise non-adjacent, and it is maximal independent when it is maximal under inclusion. For an integer i, let m.i.s.(G,i) be the number of maximal independent subsets of V(Γ(G)) having cardinality i. A subgroup H ≤ G is maximal abelian when H is abelian and every abelian subgroup K satisfying H ≤ K ≤ G equals H. Let m.a.s.(G,i) be the number of maximal abelian subgroups of G having cardinality i. Here |X| denotes cardinality, so m and all size indices are integers. The claim is: for every finite non-abelian group G and every integer m ≥ |Z(G)|, m.i.s.(G,m) = m.a.s.(G,m−|Z(G)|).
source_quote:
Let $G$ a group and $Z(G)$ the center of $G.$ The \emph{non-commuting graph} $\Gamma(G)$ associated to $G$
is the graph with vertex set $G \setminus Z(G)$ and such that two vertices $x$ and $y$ are adjacent
whenever $xy \neq yx$.

Let $G$ and $H$ be non-abelian finite groups and let $M(G)$ denote the set of orders
of maximal abelian subgroups of $G$. A subset of the vertices of a graph is called an \emph{independent set} if
its elements are pairwise non-adjacent and a subset of the vertices is a \emph{maximal
independent set} if it is maximal with respect to the inclusion.

Let $G$ be a non-commutative finite group, we define the \emph{independent polynomial of} $G$ as
\[Pi_G(x) = \sum_{i \geq 1} \mathrm{m.i.s} (G, i) x^i,\]
where $\mathrm{m.i.s} (G, i)$ is the number maximal independent sets of $V(\Gamma(G))$ of size $i.$

A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is termed \emph{maximal abelian subgroup} or a \emph{self-centralizing abelian subgroup} if it satisfies the following equivalent conditions:
\begin{itemize}
  \item $H=C_{G}(H)$, where $C_{G}(H)$ denotes the centralizer of $H$ in $G$;
  \item $C_{G}(H)H\leq H$ and $H$ is abelian;
  \item $H$ is abelian, and if $H\leq K\leq G$ with $K$ abelian, then $H=K$.
\end{itemize}

Let $G$ be a non-commutative finite group, we define the \emph{polynomial of maximal abelian subgroups of} $G$ as
\[PAS_G(x) = \sum_{i \geq 1} \mathrm{m.a.s} (G, i) x^i,\]
where $\mathrm{m.a.s} (G, i)$ is the number maximal abelian subgroups of $G$ of size $i.$

Let $G$ be a non-abelian finite group, then for all $m \geq |Z(G)|$ we have that $\mathrm{m.i.s}(G, m) = \mathrm{m.a.s}(G, m-|Z(G)|)$
